$comment: Plain titles and one-sentence summaries for every series (DESIGN.md 6.4; round 2, item: plain titles). Editorial text, never data: the printed name stays on the series as its printed label (shown as a grey second line and in About) and the full definition stays in About. Rules: a title is the words a reader would use, at most about forty characters where the series allows it, unique across the release, with no digits; siblings are told apart in words (urban, rural, women, men, a province, 'earlier base' for the index base used before the rebasing, which prints no area, and '(new definition)' for the nineteenth ICLS labour series, never joined to the others). A title never claims more than the series is: budget function lines say which part of spending they are ('current' is the revenue account; development, PSDP and capital-account lines say so), a receipts line listed under a different head says which head, an index is not a rate, a weight is not a price. A summary is one sentence of at most one hundred and thirty characters with no digits. Every entry is a draft for Ali's review ('status': 'draft'); 'drafted' says whether it was written by hand or composed by scripts/draft-titles.mjs from the series' own dims and printed names and then reviewed. scripts/checks/titles.mjs fails the build on a missing, duplicate, over-long or digit-bearing entry, or one keyed to a series the release does not hold. PROVISIONAL (unattended run, 2026-11-15): drafted by the titles agent; Ali approves, edits or replaces.
